G2, the Chicago-based software insights platform, agreed today to acquire three prominent software review and discovery properties from Gartner: Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp\.

The deal brings four of the **largest B2B review** sites under a single roof and signals a shift toward unified, AI-driven software recommendation and buying experiences\.

According to the announcement, the combined business will include roughly six million verified customer reviews and tap into an audience of more than 200 million annual software buyers\. G2 said it expects the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2026, subject to standard regulatory and closing conditions\.

G2’s leadership frames the agreement as a response to fragmentation in the software buying journey\. By consolidating multiple review databases and audiences, the company aims to streamline discovery for buyers and expand demand-generation tools for vendors\.

In a public post, G2’s CEO described the integration as building “the trusted data foundation for B2B software in the age of AI,” with deeper buyer intent signals and a more consistent taxonomy across categories\.

For buyers, the enlarged platform promises easier access to user-verified feedback and faster decision cycles\. For software vendors, the unified dataset could translate into broader visibility and enhanced market insights\.

G2’s roadmap includes tighter AI integration across search and recommendation workflows\.

Gartner, which currently owns Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp, has held these properties for years as part of its digital markets portfolio\.

This divestiture appears to reflect a strategic choice to focus its core research and advisory business while enabling specialized review platforms to evolve under a dedicated marketplace operator\.

As the software market continues to expand, the consolidation of review infrastructure under G2 could reshape how products are evaluated and purchased\.

The market will watch closely for how the combined entity leverages its scale to influence search visibility and buyer influence metrics in 2026 and beyond\.

## G2 Acquires Gartner’s ⁣Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp: Reshaping the B2B‌ software Landscape

**Published: 2026/01/29 23:13:31**

Chicago-based ⁢G2, a leading platform for software and service reviews, has announced the acquisition of Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp from Gartner\. This strategic move consolidates four major players in the B2B software review⁣ space, signaling ‌a notable shift towards AI-powered software⁢ discovery​ and purchasing experiences\. The deal, announced on january 29, ​2026, is expected to ⁣close in the first quarter of the year, pending regulatory approvals \[1\]\.

## What Does This Acquisition Mean?

The combined entity will boast a massive database of approximately six million verified customer ⁣reviews ⁣and reach an audience exceeding 200 million annual software ⁤buyers\. This scale positions G2 to become an even more dominant force in⁤ helping businesses navigate the complex world of software⁤ selection\.The ‌integration of these platforms aims to streamline the software discovery process, offering users a more thorough and data-driven approach to ⁤finding the⁣ right solutions for their needs\.

### Understanding the Platforms Involved

- **G2:** A platform‌ known for its in-depth‍ user reviews and comparison tools, focusing on providing authentic ⁣insights into software and services \[1\]\.
- **Capterra:** A free service helping businesses find the right software, offering a directory of thousands ⁤of software packages and user ‍reviews \[1\]\.
- **Software Advice:** Provides personalized software recommendations ​based⁤ on a business’s specific requirements,⁤ offering free consultations with software‌ advisors \[1\]\.
- **GetApp:** Focuses on helping businesses discover and compare software, particularly for small‍ and medium-sized businesses \[1\]\.

## The Rise of AI⁢ in Software Discovery

G2’s acquisition of these platforms isn’t⁣ just about scale; it’s about leveraging ⁤the power of⁣ artificial intelligence\. The company intends to integrate AI capabilities across the combined platforms to deliver more personalized and predictive software recommendations\. This includes using machine learning to analyze user reviews, identify emerging trends, and match​ businesses with the software‍ that best‌ fits their ⁣needs\. According to G2’s help center\[2\], the platform gathers and publishes unbiased user reviews to‌ help professionals make informed decisions\.

## Impact ⁣on the B2B Software Market

this consolidation is expected to have a significant impact on the B2B software ​market\.⁤ By bringing‍ together these four major ⁣review sites,⁤ G2 aims to create a ‍more unified and efficient ‍software buying experiance\. This could lead⁤ to⁢ increased clarity, reduced friction in the sales ‌process, and ultimately, better software choices for businesses of all sizes\. The move also signals a growing​ trend towards data-driven decision-making in the software industry, where user reviews and ​independent analysis are becoming‍ increasingly significant\.

## Key Takeaways

- G2 ⁣has acquired Capterra,‌ Software Advice, and GetApp ⁤from⁤ Gartner\.
- The deal creates a leading‍ platform with six‌ million verified ‍reviews and a reach of over 200 million buyers\.
- AI will play ‍a central role in enhancing ​software discovery and ⁤proposal capabilities\.
- The acquisition⁢ is expected to streamline the B2B software buying process\.

Looking ahead,the integration of these platforms will⁣ be crucial\. G2 will ‍need to effectively combine ‌the ​strengths of⁣ each platform while maintaining the trust and credibility that⁣ each has​ built with its‌ user base\. The ⁢success ⁤of this acquisition will ultimately depend on G2’s ability to deliver a truly seamless and ‍valuable experience for software buyers\.

#### *Convenient PIX payments via Unlimit will enable GetApps to serve millions of potential customers *

LONDON, UK – Media OutReach Newswire** **– 26 March 2024 –** ** Unlimit, a leading global fintech company, today announced it has partnered with Xiaomi, one of the world’s leading consumer electronics and smart manufacturing companies, to strengthen the expansion of Xiaomi’s GetApps, the company’s app distribution platform for international markets in Brazil\. By providing PIX, Unlimit will greatly simplify the payment process for GetApps’ local customers, and support GetApps’ development goals in the region\.

Unlimit’s powerful proprietary payments infrastructure, global acquiring capabilities, and portfolio of over 1,000 directly integrated payment methods, made the company a great fit for GetApps ambitious LATAM expansion plans\. The platform will now accept PIX, one of Brazil’s most popular payment methods, expanding its reach to millions of potential customers\.

GetApps, owned by the International Internet Business Department of Xiaomi, is Xiaomi’s official app store for its international market, which operates in over 90 markets and connects developers with millions of users in the most lucrative regions\. Unlimit is a global, award-winning all-in-one fintech offering advanced payment capabilities to businesses worldwide, with 16 offices across four continents\. Their mission is to eliminate financial borders and help businesses grow globally\.

Unlimit will continue to support GetApps with additional payment capabilities, enabling them to further solidify their foothold in the Latin American market\.

**Commenting on the expansion, Irene Skrynova, Chief Customer Officer, at Unlimit said: **

“We are honoured to be a part of this exciting journey together with Xiaomi’s GetApps and to support them on this strategically important next step focused on strengthening its presence in LATAM\. For more than 15 years our main focus has always been the provision of world-class payment solutions, that seamlessly support our customers in their local and cross-border expansions, guaranteeing a truly “borderless” approach to payments\. We are certain that our partnership will help to further unveil GetApps’ potential in the region, by delivering a stable, smooth and diverse payment experience to the end users\.”

# Android Without Google: Your VPN Options

A VPN for de-Googled Android is entirely doable; running Android without Google Play does not lock you out of one\. It only changes how you install it\.

Instead of a single store, you have three routes: an open-source repository like F-Droid, a direct APK from the provider, or an alternative app store\.

- **Some apps lean on Google for push\.** A few VPN apps use Google’s push service for notifications, which can misbehave without Play Services, though the core tunnel still works\.
- **Updates become manual, sometimes\.** A direct-APK install does not auto-update, so you either check by hand or use a tool that watches for new releases\.
- **Sideloading needs a toggle\.** Installing an APK requires allowing installs from the source, a permission you grant once\.

None of this stops a VPN from running\. It just decides which of the three routes below you take\.

## **F-Droid and Open-Source Repositories**

The purist route\. F-Droid is a catalogue of free and open-source apps, and it is pre-installed on de-Googled systems like CalyxOS\. If a VPN is here, it is the cleanest install a privacy-focused user can make\.

1. **Mullvad** is the standout, and honesty demands naming it\. It is on F-Droid, its apps are open source, and the GrapheneOS project specifically names it as a recommended VPN because it is tested with hardware memory tagging\. For pure privacy on a de-Googled phone, it is the consensus pick\.

The limit of this route is selection\. Few commercial VPNs publish to F-Droid, so the catalogue is small and weighted toward the privacy-maximalist names, which tend to be WireGuard-only\.

## **Direct APK From the Provider**

The universal route, and the one that works for almost any VPN\. To install VPN without Play Store access of any kind, this is the path that never fails\. You download the APK file straight from the provider’s official website and install it, which sidesteps every store entirely\.

1. **Most major VPNs** also offer a direct APK, including NordVPN, Surfshark and Proton, though you take on manual updating in exchange\.

The rule for this route is discipline about the source\. A VPN APK Android download is only as safe as where it comes from, so use the provider’s own domain and never a third-party mirror like APKPure or APKMirror\.

- **Obtainium** is not a store but a tool that installs and updates apps straight from their GitHub releases, useful for open-source VPNs\.

This route gives you store-style convenience and automatic updates while keeping Google out, which is why it suits a de-Googled phone that still wants low-friction installs\.

## **Which VPN Actually Fits a De-Googled Phone**

The right choice depends on which of two things you want most: maximum privacy, or obfuscation and install flexibility\.

# Google Play removes VK and Max apps amid EU sanctions escalation

Google Play has removed applications from Russian tech giant VK and its Max messenger following EU sanctions, highlighting how geopolitical measures are reshaping access to Russian digital services\.\.\.

Google Play has removed applications from Russian tech giant VK and its Max messenger following EU sanctions, highlighting how geopolitical measures are reshaping access to Russian digital services internationally\.

Google Play has removed applications from Russian technology group VK and its Max messenger from its Android store, marking the latest sign of pressure on the company’s digital services after fresh European Union sanctions\. VK said the restriction applies only to new downloads, while existing users can continue using the apps without disruption\.

According to VK, people who already have the software installed should still receive push notifications for messages, events and calls, and the services remain usable on Android devices\. The company also said it is trying to preserve access for users and is directing them to alternative ways of installing and updating the applications\.

The Google Play move follows a similar step by Apple, which removed VK-related apps from the App Store at the end of June\. Meduza reported that the latest removals came three days after the EU sanctioned VK, along with a subsidiary linked to the development of Max, broadening the impact of the bloc’s measures across major international platforms\.

For sanctions and trade-control readers, Noah Intelligence and Noah Wire help track how designations, platform restrictions and cross-border compliance pressure can reshape access to digital services across jurisdictions\.

Other reports said the apps remain available through Russian and other Android app stores, including RuStore, Huawei AppGallery, Samsung Galaxy Store and Xiaomi GetApps\. The episode underlines how sanctions are increasingly shaping the reach of Russian digital products abroad, even as VK has positioned Max as part of Moscow’s push for home-grown alternatives to Western technology\.

# BeEzrat HaShem Inc\. Receives Candid Platinum Seal for Third Consecutive Year

**HOLLYWOOD, FL**** ***Torah education nonprofit maintains Candid’s highest transparency rating and reports its 2025 program outcomes*

BeEzrat HaShem Inc\., a Florida-based 501\(c\)\(3\) Torah education and outreach organization, has received Candid’s 2026 Platinum Seal of Transparency for the third consecutive year\.

BeEzrat HaShem Inc\.

The Platinum Seal is the highest of Candid’s four transparency designations\. According to the organization, fewer than 1% of the approximately 1\.8 million U\.S\. nonprofits listed in Candid’s database have achieved the Platinum level\.

“Earning Platinum once shows that an organization can prepare a strong report\. Earning it three years in a row demonstrates that transparency is part of how we operate,” said Rabbi Yaron Reuven, founder and president of BeEzrat HaShem Inc\. “Our donors support us because they trust us to spread Torah, perform chesed, and help feed people in need\. That trust is sacred, and the Platinum Seal allows us to demonstrate through publicly reported data how donations are being used\.”

Candid’s Platinum designation requires participating nonprofits to disclose measurable program outcomes in addition to information about their finances, governance, mission, and operations\. Organizations must review and update their profiles annually to maintain the designation\.

2026 Platinum Seal of Transparency

3 Years Platinum · Top 1% U\.S\. Nonprofits

Candid has also reported that nonprofits displaying a Seal of Transparency receive, on average, 62% more donor contributions than organizations without a seal\.

#### **2025 Program Results Reported to Candid**

BeEzrat HaShem Inc\. reported the following results for 2025:

- Raised $2\.3 million, primarily through individual donors who discovered the organization through its online Torah education programs rather than through foundation grants\.
- Provided food or financial assistance to approximately 238,000 Jewish individuals\.
- Produced and distributed more than 15,000 Torah lectures and over 500 Torah-based films\.
- Operated 23 YouTube channels in 15 languages, reaching more than 200,000 combined subscribers and followers\.
- Distributed more than 280,000 complimentary copies of 36 sefarim authored by co-founder Rabbi Efraim Kachlon, compared with 150,000 copies distributed in 2024\.
- Distributed more than 2\.3 million outreach materials, including CDs, USB drives, and kiruv cards, at no charge\.
- Supported religious scholarship infrastructure consisting of two kollels for Dayanut, one Beit Din, and 12 rabbis and speakers\.
- Developed and operated two proprietary platforms: the free BH Torah lecture app at www\.BeEzratHaShem\.org/getapp and the AI Rabbi question-and-answer platform at www\.AIRabbi\.org\.
- Launched the Teshuva Music and BH Kids YouTube channels, featuring original kosher educational and entertainment content\.

“Many nonprofits of our size do not pursue the Platinum designation because of the level of documentation required,” Rabbi Reuven said\. “We continue to pursue it because our supporters deserve clear, measurable information showing that we are responsible stewards of their donations\.”

BeEzrat HaShem Inc\. uses individual donations to support Torah education, religious book publishing, digital educational resources, and chesed programs\.

Additional information about the organization and its programs is available at www\.BeEzratHaShem\.org\. Donations can be made at www\.BeEzratHaShem\.org/donate\. The organization’s verified Candid Nonprofit Profile is also available through Candid\.

#### **About BeEzrat HaShem Inc\.**

BeEzrat HaShem Inc\. is a Florida-based 501\(c\)\(3\) nonprofit organization focused on Torah education, outreach, publishing, and chesed initiatives\. The organization operates 23 YouTube channels in 15 languages, two proprietary digital applications, multiple educational websites, and a global complimentary book-distribution program\. BeEzrat HaShem Inc\. was founded by Rabbi Yaron Reuven and co-founded by Rabbi Efraim Kachlon\. Its activities are funded primarily by individual donors who engage with the organization’s online Torah education programs\.

# VK’s apps and MAX messenger removed from Google Play amid EU sanctions

Russian internet group VK and its MAX messenger have disappeared from Google Play following EU sanctions, but existing users face no disruption as services remain accessible through alternative stores and the Russian\.\.\.

Russian internet group VK and its MAX messenger have disappeared from Google Play following EU sanctions, but existing users face no disruption as services remain accessible through alternative stores and the Russian domain\.

VK’s apps and its MAX messenger have disappeared from Google Play, although the Russian internet group says existing users have not been disrupted\. In a statement cited by Interfax, the company said previously installed services continue to work normally, including push notifications for messages, events and calls on Android devices, and that updates remain available through in-app prompts or alternative app stores\.

The removals affect a broad range of VK products, not just its flagship social network and messenger\. According to reporting in Russian and international outlets, Google Play no longer shows VKontakte, Odnoklassniki, Dzen, VK Messenger, VK Calls, VK Dating, VK Music, VK Video, VK Video Live and VK Clips, alongside Mail\.ru Mail, Mail\.ru Cloud, VK Mail, VK WorkSpace, VK Play, Yula and Marusya\. VK says users can still install and update its apps through stores such as RuStore, Huawei AppGallery, Samsung Galaxy Store and Xiaomi GetApps\.

The timing points to the latest round of European Union sanctions, which came into force on 13 July and directly targeted VK and the company behind MAX, Communicating Platform\. The EU has argued that MAX was shaped by Russia’s security services and could collect device, contact and location data, monitor VPN use and push updates itself\. Brussels has also accused VK of passing user data to authorities and helping to restrict VPN access\.

VK has rejected the suggestion that the sanctions would affect day-to-day use of its services, saying they would remain available in their usual form\. At the same time, the company has begun steering users away from the long-standing vk\.com domain and towards vk\.ru, saying the Russian address is faster and more stable while the service itself remains unchanged\. VK has also indicated that it will support access to its services only through the \.ru domain going forward\.

The Google Play removals follow an earlier wave of restrictions from Apple\. In late June, Apple removed several VK apps from the App Store, including VK Video, VK Messenger, VK Music and Dzen, citing sanctions compliance, while MAX also vanished earlier that month\. The latest step shows how quickly sanctions pressure is now reshaping distribution for Russian consumer apps across both major mobile ecosystems\.
